name: Lhotse Expedition
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province; Sagarmatha National Park; Nepal-Tibet border (main summit)

difficulty.notes: Fourth-highest mountain. Standard commercial line shares Everest through the Khumbu Icefall, Western Cwm and Lhotse Face to about Camp 3; the routes split before Everest's South Col. Lhotse Camp 4 sits near the Geneva Spur / 'Turtle'; the summit crux is the Lhotse Couloir (steep snow/ice, conditions snow-dependent). Supplemental oxygen is normal on commercial teams. South Face is a separate, rarely commercial route. Prior 7,000-8,000 m experience is typically required by operators.

duration_days.notes: Seven Summit Treks lists 60 days; Adventure Consultants 2026 was 54 days (7 Apr-30 May). Combined Everest+Lhotse programmes add a second summit push after Everest. Permit validity reportedly shortened 75 to 55 days (UNVERIFIED beyond Everest reporting).

max_altitude_point: Lhotse Main summit (Lhotse Shar 8,383 m and Lhotse Middle/East 8,413 m are separate summits)
start_point: Kathmandu (fly to Lukla, or via Manthali/Ramechhap in peak seasons)

itinerary.route: Arrive Kathmandu; DoT briefing, permits, gear check
Fly Lukla; trek Phakding - Namche (rest) - Deboche/Tengboche - Dingboche - Lobuche - Everest/Lhotse Base Camp
itinerary.notes: Shares Everest Base Camp on the Khumbu Glacier (operators also list about 5,400 m). Some teams add Kongma La or Lobuche East for acclimatisation.

itinerary.route: Puja; Icefall ladder training; move through Icefall to Camp 1
itinerary.notes: Camp 1 about 5,900-6,100 m above the Icefall.

itinerary.route: Rotations: Camp 1 - Western Cwm - Camp 2 - Lhotse Face - touch/sleep Camp 3 - return to Base Camp; rest awaiting weather
itinerary.notes: Camp 2 about 6,400-6,750 m (operator spread); Camp 3 about 7,100-7,300 m on the Lhotse Face. Everest and Lhotse teams share the line to the Yellow Band.

itinerary.route: Summit window (typically mid-late May): Base Camp - Camp 2 - Camp 3 (oxygen) - Camp 4 near Geneva Spur (about 7,800-7,900 m) - Lhotse Couloir - summit 8,516 m - descend to Camp 2 / Base Camp
itinerary.walking_hours: Summit day about 6-8 h from Camp 4 (Adventure Consultants); SST cites 7-8 h
itinerary.notes: Spring 2026: EOAN/SST rope-fixing team reached the Lhotse summit on 17 May.

itinerary.route: SPCC garbage checks; trek Base Camp - Pheriche - Namche - Lukla
itinerary.notes: Helicopter descent used by some teams.

best_seasons.notes: Commercial Lhotse is a spring peak sharing Everest's Icefall calendar. Autumn and winter ascents exist but are uncommon. First winter ascent: 31 December 1988, Krzysztof Wielicki.

permits.name: Department of Tourism climbing royalty - other mountains above 8,000 m (includes Lhotse)
permits.fee: USD 3,000 per person spring (Mar-May); USD 1,500 autumn (Sep-Nov); USD 750 winter/summer

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (refundable, per expedition team) - other 8,000 m in Khumbu
Khumbu Icefall route fee (Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee)
permits.fee: USD 600 per foreign climber (Everest, Lhotse and Nuptse permit holders)

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)

guide_requirements: Sixth Amendment: solo expeditions on all 8,000 m peaks banned; at least one mountain guide or high-altitude worker for every two members. Government liaison officer attached. Staff insurance minimums: NPR 2,000,000 for mountain guides/high-altitude workers, NPR 1,500,000 for liaison officers and base-camp workers. Climber insurance copy required with the permit application. SPCC 2026 waste rules at Everest BC apply (8 kg carry-down including 2 kg from above Camp 2; municipality poop bags above BC).

flights: Kathmandu - Lukla, or Manthali-Lukla in peak windows
drives: Kathmandu - Manthali when Lukla flights are diverted
logistics.notes: Teahouses on the approach; full-service tented Base Camp shared with Everest; high camps on the Icefall/Cwm/Face. Icefall Doctors' route is the same as Everest's.

highlights: Fourth-highest summit, 8,516 m, connected to Everest by the South Col
Lhotse Couloir as the summit crux
Shared Khumbu Icefall and Western Cwm with Everest, with far fewer people above Camp 3
First ascent 18 May 1956, Fritz Luchsinger and Ernst Reiss (Swiss Everest/Lhotse expedition)
risks: Khumbu Icefall serac collapse and avalanche
Lhotse Face ice and the Couloir in poor snow
Extreme altitude: HAPE, HACE, hypoxia, oxygen failure
Objective hazard on the South Face if that variant is used

acclimatization.notes: Same rotation pattern as Everest: Icefall familiarisation, nights at Camps 1-2, touch Camp 3, rest at Base Camp, then a weather-window push.

unverified: Permit validity cut from 75 to 55 days: reported for Everest; not independently confirmed as applying to Lhotse.
Camp 2 altitude: Adventure Consultants 6,400 m; SST page states both 6,750 m and 6,500 m.
Icefall Doctors team fee sometimes quoted separately from the USD 600 per-climber SPCC fee.
Whether a combined Everest+Lhotse climber pays two full royalties plus one Icefall fee (operator practice; confirm at booking).
